children: Czech-based Agrofert Group's AGF Nitrogen said on Wednesday it was considering reducing ammonia output at its European plants due to high prices of natural gas and carbon emission allowances.

"As natural gas prices continue to rise and emissions allowance prices remain several times higher than in the rest of the world, ammonia and the fertilizers produced from it are reaching again a price level that is becoming unaffordable for European farmers," Chief Executive Petr Cingr of AGF Nitrogen, which says that it is Europe's second-largest producer of fertilisers and nitrogen-based products, said in a statement.
